settings.question: Why did my MacBook suddenly die with no liquid spill or drop?
settings.answer: Sudden no-power failures on MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models are commonly caused by a shorted surface-mount capacitor on the main power rail, a failed USB-C charging IC (such as a CD3217 controller), or a power management fault after voltage spikes or third-party chargers. These can usually be traced and repaired at component level without replacing the whole logic board.

settings.question: Will I lose my data if my MacBook won't turn on?
settings.answer: Because modern MacBooks have the SSD soldered directly onto the logic board, Apple's standard logic board replacement wipes all data. By repairing the power circuit on your original logic board, we aim to restore your MacBook with your files and apps completely intact.

settings.question: Apple quoted £700+ for a new logic board. Can iCorrect give me a second opinion?
settings.answer: Yes. Many of our dead MacBook repairs come directly from clients who received a high logic board replacement quote from an Apple Store or authorised centre. Book our diagnostic and we will inspect the board under the microscope within 1 working day and email a clear written report and fixed component-level quote.

settings.question: Do you repair dead M1, M2, M3, and M4 Apple Silicon MacBooks?
settings.answer: Yes. Our Fitzrovia workshop repairs both Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4) and Intel MacBook Air and MacBook Pro logic boards, including USB-C / MagSafe charging failures, DFU firmware recovery, and power-rail short circuits.

settings.question: How long does a dead MacBook logic board repair take?
settings.answer: Once your MacBook reaches our workshop, we complete the full power-rail diagnostic and email your written quote within 1 working day. Standard repairs complete within 2 working days once approved, with exact timing confirmed upfront for complex board faults.

settings.question: What warranty covers a no-power logic board repair?
